detailed_rationale:
Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services operates a network of multi-specialty hospitals concentrated in the Delhi-NCR belt (Noida, Greater Noida, and other locations), a smaller and younger chain than majors like Narayana or Apollo, still in an earlier, faster-growth expansion phase. Q1 FY27 (Jun-2026 quarter) results were strong and consistent with the quant data's very high growth scores: revenue grew in the mid-20s percent YoY, net income grew faster (roughly high-30s percent), EPS rose from Rs 3.54 to Rs 4.36, and profit margin improved from 14% to 16%. Importantly, this is not simply bed-count growth - group ARPOB (average revenue per occupied bed) rose 5% YoY to Rs 33,283, explicitly attributed to a higher share of high-value specialties, with the flagship Noida Extension and Greater Noida hospitals posting well-above-average ARPOB (Rs 47.8k and Rs 40.3k respectively). That is a genuine quality-of-growth signal: revenue per bed is rising because the case mix is shifting toward more complex, higher-value care as these hospitals mature, not purely because more beds were added.

Unlike some names in this batch, Yatharth's growth does not show the classic base-effect divergence pattern - the 3-year revenue CAGR (36.2%) and 1-year growth (36.1%) are closely aligned, meaning this is a sustained, multi-year growth trajectory rather than a one-quarter or one-year spike against a weak base. That consistency is a meaningfully better growth-quality signal than a name where trailing 1-year growth wildly outstrips the 3-year trend.

The quant quality_score (54.3) is more middling than the growth scores (89.5/88.2) would suggest a hospital chain should command, which likely reflects Yatharth's smaller scale, geographic concentration (NCR-heavy, less diversified than pan-India peers), and a still-maturing return profile (ROE 16.7%, ROCE 19.3% - respectable but below the strongest listed hospital peers). At ~47x trailing earnings, the valuation already prices in continued strong execution; this is a name where the growth story is genuinely intact based on current evidence, but the multiple leaves limited room for a hospital-capex-cycle slowdown or any execution stumble as newer facilities ramp.
recommendation_rationale: Quant score is Hold. The growth story here is more genuine (consistent 3yr/1yr trend, quality-of-growth support from rising ARPOB and mix shift) than several other names in this batch, but the valuation (~47x) already reflects that strength and the quality_score flags real scale/concentration limitations - so there is no basis to push beyond Hold, nor any reason to be more cautious than Hold given the clean growth trend.
summary: Yatharth Hospital continues to post strong, consistent growth - revenue up in the mid-20s percent and profit up faster, aided by hospitals maturing into higher-value specialty care rather than just adding beds. This is one of the more genuine growth stories in this review, with three-year and one-year growth trends closely aligned rather than showing a one-off spike. The stock's valuation already reflects much of this strength, and the company remains smaller and more geographically concentrated (Delhi-NCR) than the larger hospital chains, which caps how much further re-rating room may exist.
positive_para: Growth here is unusually well-supported by quality-of-growth evidence: ARPOB is rising as the hospital network's case mix shifts toward higher-value specialties, and three-year and one-year growth rates are closely aligned (36% both), reducing the risk that the trailing growth score is a base-effect artifact. Profit is growing faster than revenue (margin improving from 14% to 16%), and flagship hospitals show ARPOB well above the group average, indicating the network is maturing well.
negative_para: Yatharth remains smaller in scale and more geographically concentrated (Delhi-NCR-centric) than the larger listed hospital chains, which is likely reflected in its more middling quality_score (54.3) despite exceptional growth scores - single-region concentration is a real risk if that specific market softens or faces new competitive hospital capacity. At ~47x trailing earnings, the valuation already assumes this strong growth persists; any slowdown as the network matures (natural deceleration as more hospitals move from ramp-up to steady-state) or execution missteps in further expansion would compress both earnings growth and the multiple together.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~47x trailing earnings for a hospital chain still growing revenue and profit in the mid-30s percent with genuine mix-driven ARPOB support, the multiple is demanding but not obviously disconnected from the growth on offer - unlike some peers in this review, the growth here is not a base-effect illusion. The key risk to the multiple is natural deceleration as bed capacity additions mature into steady-state utilization rather than any current red flag; call this fair value for a genuine, if geographically concentrated, growth story.
